title: Session expiry, password recovery, and unauthenticated deep links
asA: user whose session lapsed or who lost a password
iWant: recovery paths that keep my place and my data
soThat: an expired session or forgotten password is a detour, not a dead end

acceptanceCriteria.description: When a request returns 401 mid-session, the session-expired surface renders per its wireframe, naming what happened; the user is not dumped onto the landing page without explanation.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an authenticated user whose session expires

acceptanceCriteria.description: Re-authenticating from the session-expired surface returns the user to the route they were on, with unsaved form input preserved where the journey specification declares preservation.
acceptanceCriteria.then: they land back on the same route with declared preservation honoured

acceptanceCriteria.description: Forgot-password is linked from sign-in, confirms the request without disclosing whether the account exists, and states what happens next.
acceptanceCriteria.when: a known and an unknown address are submitted
acceptanceCriteria.then: both render the same designed confirmation

acceptanceCriteria.description: The account-recovery surface validates the recovery token, renders a designed invalid-or-expired-token state with a restart path, and applies the application-spa-REQ-007 contract to the new-credential form.
acceptanceCriteria.given: valid, invalid, and expired recovery links
acceptanceCriteria.then: valid proceeds; invalid and expired render the designed state with a restart path

acceptanceCriteria.description: Visiting a protected deep link while unauthenticated redirects to sign-in and, on success, forwards to the originally requested route.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an unauthenticated visit to a protected route

acceptanceCriteria.description: The deep-link return target is validated to be an in-application route; external or malformed targets fall back to the default authenticated route.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a crafted redirect target pointing outside the application
acceptanceCriteria.then: the user lands on the default route, never an external URL
